## X polls

- A poll is its own content type, `ContentType::XPoll` (`x_poll`), with `meta.poll = {options, duration_minutes}` (owner decision November 2026). `App\Support\Social\XPoll` is the one home for its rules (constants, `limits()`, `options()` / `choices()`, `normalize()`, `violation()`, `optionsCountViolation()`, `choiceLengthViolation()`, `requiredViolation()`, `questionViolation()`, `payload()`, `result()`, `fromPublication()`); `PostPlatformMetaRules`, `PostMeta::forChannel()` / `PostMeta::merge()`, `PostCompositionValidator`, `ContentType::maxContentLengthFor()`, `ThreadReplies` and `XPublisher` call it, never a copy of the numbers or messages. X's `voting_status` values are `App\Enums\X\PollVotingStatus`.
- 2–4 choices of 1–25 characters counted as X counts them (UTF-16 units, so an emoji like 🐧 counts two: `XPoll::choiceLength()`, mirrored by `pollChoiceLength()`; X refused a choice of 25 code points holding one), a duration of 5–10080 minutes, and a question (the post text) of at most 280 characters, even on an account with long posts. Blank choices are dropped and duplicates refused. `PostMeta::forChannel()` drops `poll` on any other type.
- A poll carries no media. A poll with fewer than two choices, or without a question, is a draft that cannot be scheduled (the question error replaces the generic "content or media" one); `XPublisher` refuses it, and refuses stored media with `posts.errors.media_not_accepted`.
- **Any post of a thread can be a poll, several in one thread** (owner decision November 2026: X allows a poll on a reply). The root is a poll through its content type (`x_poll`, `meta.poll`); a reply stays `XPost` and carries its poll in the reply itself: `meta.thread_replies.*` is `{text, media, poll}`, `poll` under the same rules as `meta.poll` (`PostPlatformMetaRules`), the reply text as its question (at most 280 characters even with long posts), no media (refused at every save by `ThreadReplies::pollMediaErrors()`). `ThreadReplies` holds the reply rules (`pollFormatViolation()` at every save, `violation()` before scheduling), calling `XPoll`, whose helpers read `poll.*` from a post's meta or a reply alike. Off X, `PostMeta::forChannel()` drops reply polls (`ThreadReplies::withoutPolls()`). `PublishesThreads` passes each reply's poll to the publisher and into its checkpoint hash (a reply without one keeps its old hash). In the composer the root keeps the Post | Poll picker; an active X reply turns into a poll with the toolbar's poll button (`ComposerEditorToolbar`, off with the media reason while the reply has media), and its poll editor (`XPollField` with `field-prefix` `thread_replies.{n}.` and its own test ids) shows while that reply is edited.
- Attaching media through the API or MCP to a poll is refused by one guard, `AppendPostMedia::ensureAcceptsMedia()`: `execute()` always runs it, and the entry points that store or download a file first (`PostController::storeMedia`, `MediaAttacher::attachFromUrls`) call it before doing so.
- **Cost rule (owner decision):** polls and their votes ride on requests X already makes. Never add a request, job or schedule for polls.
    - Results are read by `XPublicationMetricsCollector` in the existing X metrics read (`GET /2/tweets/{id}`), on its usual schedule (about an hour after publishing, then at the ages in `SyncCadence::X_METRICS_DAYS`), into `analytics_publications.provider_metadata.poll`, without moving `updated_at`. A read without a poll leaves the stored one alone.
    - When TryPost published reply polls, the same read becomes one `GET /2/tweets?ids={post},{replies with a poll}` (owner decision November 2026: still one request, though X bills each extra post it returns), and their results go to `provider_metadata.thread_polls`, a list of `{reply, ...result}` where `reply` is the reply's position from 0 (matched through `posts.thread_reply_ids`). Discovery excludes replies, so it never sees them; `UpsertAnalyticsPublication` merges `provider_metadata` key by key so a rediscovery keeps them.
    - A poll made on x.com is found by `XPublicationCollector`'s existing discovery request, which writes the same `provider_metadata.poll`, and typed `PublicationContentType::Poll`, which `ContentType::fromPublication()` maps to `x_poll` for the importer and the insights type filter (a poll TryPost published is stored as `Poll` by `SyncTryPostPublication`). `provider_metadata.poll` is the one home of a poll's result; there is no column of its own.
- Results are exposed as `publication.poll` and `publication.thread_polls` (read from `provider_metadata`) by `ReadPublicationAnalytics` (web, API, MCP) and shown by `PostPollResults.vue` in the Sent tab and post details, a reply's poll captioned with its post number (`posts.poll_results.thread_post`). The API and MCP post preview (`PostPreviewer`) shows the post's poll and each reply's. Because results are not read daily, it says "Final results" only when the stored `voting_status` is `closed`; an open poll whose end has passed says "Voting ended", and one still running says when it ends.
- The duration defaults to 1440 minutes (one day, `XPoll::DEFAULT_DURATION`). The limits reach the composer through `Platform::publishConfig()` (`publishConfig.poll`, from `XPoll::limits()`), read from `platformConfigs[account.id]` by `XPollField.vue`, the X preview and the question cap; do not copy them into TypeScript. `resources/js/lib/xPoll.ts` keeps only pure helpers that take the limits as arguments; the poll types (`XPoll`, `XPollLimits`, `XPollDuration`) are in `resources/js/types/x.ts`. The composer's poll state, its limits, the type switch (`setGroupContentType`), Remove poll and the reply text limit live in `composables/composer/useComposerPoll.ts`; the media button's reason stays in `PostComposerDialog.vue`, and the medialess types (poll, Threads ghost post) with their reasons in `MEDIALESS_CONTENT_TYPE_REASONS` (`types/content-type.ts`, next to `CAPTIONLESS_CONTENT_TYPES`; `maxMediaCount()` is 0 for both on the server).
- **The poll's media rules are X poll only** (owner decision November 2026): refusing media on a draft (`PostCompositionValidator`), refusing an attach (`AppendPostMedia::ensureAcceptsMedia()`), turning a card back into a post when the shared step opens (`watch(sharedStep)` in `PostComposerDialog.vue`) and leaving the type out of the repurpose picker all test `ContentType::XPoll`, never "a type that takes no media": a Threads ghost post keeps the behaviour it had before polls (its media is refused when it is scheduled or published).
- A poll is never a repurpose destination: the repurpose requests refuse `x_poll` (`RepurposeRules`, `supportsVideo()`), and the repurpose picker (`ChannelConfigurator.vue`) leaves it out.
